_meta.what: The tactic ideas the daily plan teaches, one a day, in ladder order. `median` is the typical Lichess puzzle rating of the theme, measured 2026-11-18 on a 30,000-puzzle sample of lichess_puzzles. The question never claims the idea is on the board now: the puzzle's line uses it, and the grader checks the first move.

themes.title: Back-rank mate
themes.idea: A king behind its own pawns on the back row has no way out. A rook or queen that reaches that row gives mate.

themes.title: Smothered mate
themes.idea: A king boxed in by its own pieces cannot step away. A knight check can then be mate, because nothing can block a knight.

themes.title: Checkmate in one
themes.idea: Before any other move, look at every check you have. One of them may end the game.
themes.question: Find the move that gives checkmate.

themes.title: Opera mate
themes.idea: A rook gives mate on the edge of the board. A bishop from far away guards the square the rook stands on.

themes.title: Pillsbury's mate
themes.idea: A rook gives the mate while a bishop, often from the long diagonal, takes away the king's last square.

themes.title: The weak f-pawn
themes.idea: Early in the game, the pawn beside the king on f2 or f7 is guarded only by the king. An attack on that square often wins quickly.

themes.title: Epaulette mate
themes.idea: A king with its own pieces on both sides cannot step sideways. A check from straight in front can then be mate.

themes.title: Mate in two
themes.idea: A first move that forces the reply, often a check or a sacrifice, can set up mate on the next move.
themes.question: Mate in two. Find the first move.

themes.title: Swallow's tail mate
themes.idea: A queen checks right in front of the king, guarded by another piece. The king's own pieces block the squares behind it.

themes.title: Hook mate
themes.idea: A rook gives mate next to the king. A knight guards the rook, and a pawn guards the knight.

themes.title: Skewer
themes.idea: Attack a valuable piece that has a weaker one behind it on the same line. When the valuable piece moves, the one behind it can be taken.

themes.title: Fork
themes.idea: One piece attacks two things at once. Your opponent can save only one of them.

themes.title: Free pieces
themes.idea: A piece that nobody guards can be taken for free. Before every move, check what is unguarded, on both sides.
themes.question: Something here can be won. Find the first move.

themes.title: Discovered attack
themes.idea: Moving one piece opens a line for another piece behind it. Now two pieces attack at once.

themes.title: Promotion
themes.idea: A pawn that reaches the last row becomes a queen. Clearing the way for a pawn can win the game.

themes.title: X-ray
themes.idea: A piece can attack or guard through another piece on the same line. When the piece in between goes, the line works again.

themes.title: Deflection
themes.idea: Force a defending piece to move away. What it was guarding is then left open.

themes.title: The pawn near the end
themes.idea: A pawn close to the last row is very strong. Pushing it, or stopping it, is often the whole point of the position.

themes.title: Discovered check
themes.idea: A piece steps out of the way and uncovers a check from the piece behind it. While the king deals with the check, the piece that moved can take something.

themes.title: Pin
themes.idea: A piece cannot move without exposing a more valuable piece behind it. A pinned piece is a weak piece: attack it.

themes.title: Sacrifice
themes.idea: Give up material on purpose to get something bigger back: a mate, or more material a few moves later.

themes.title: Attraction
themes.idea: Force an enemy piece, often the king, onto a square where it can be attacked. Usually you give up a piece to do it.

themes.title: The in-between move
themes.idea: Before the move everyone expects, such as taking back, play a stronger move first: a check or a bigger threat.

themes.title: Remove the guard
themes.idea: Take the piece that guards something. What it guarded can then be taken.

themes.title: Double check
themes.idea: Two pieces give check at the same time. Blocking or taking cannot stop both, so the king must move.

themes.title: Interference
themes.idea: Put a piece between an enemy piece and what it guards. The line is cut, and the guard stops working.

themes.title: The open king
themes.idea: A king with few pieces or pawns around it is easy to attack. Bring your pieces toward it.

themes.title: Trapped piece
themes.idea: A piece with no safe square to go to can be attacked and won.

themes.title: Clearance
themes.idea: Move a piece out of the way, often with a threat, so another piece can use its square or its line.

themes.title: Zugzwang
themes.idea: Sometimes every move makes a position worse. Make the move that leaves your opponent in that spot.

themes.title: The defensive move
themes.idea: Not every position has an attack for you. Sometimes the best move stops your opponent's threat.
themes.question: The right move here is a defensive one. Find it.

themes.title: The quiet move
themes.idea: A strong move does not have to check or capture. It can set up a threat your opponent cannot meet.
